content: Hennepin County Medical Center (HCMC) is a Level I trauma center located in Minneapolis, Minnesota, which serves as the county seat of Hennepin County. The main hospital facility has 422 beds and spans five city blocks, situated across the street from the Hubert H. Humphrey Metrodome. HCMC also operates satellite clinics in Minneapolis, Brooklyn Center, and Richfield. Since 1999, it has consistently been recognized as one of America's Best Hospitals by U.S. News & World Report. Patients often travel significant distances to receive care at HCMC due to its renowned trauma surgery specialists, transplant services, advanced endoscopy and hepatobiliary center, and the region's only hyperbaric oxygen chamber. The hospital was originally established in 1887 as the Minneapolis City Hospital, also known as General Hospital or City Hospital, located a block from its current site. Ownership was transferred to Hennepin County in 1964, at which point it was renamed Hennepin County General Hospital. It adopted its current name in 1974. By the early 1970s, the hospital's facilities had become a disorganized collection of buildings, prompting a decision to rebuild. The current hospital structure was completed in 1976, funded by a $25 million bond approved by voters in 1969. In 1991, the hospital expanded after the closure of the adjacent Metropolitan-Mount Sinai Medical Center. HCMC achieved Level I trauma center designation in 1989, becoming the first such facility in Minnesota. In January 2007, the hospital underwent a governance change, creating a new governing entity with greater autonomy from county government. This transition aimed to ensure the hospital's long-term viability while maintaining its public mission. HCMC offers independent residency programs in Emergency Medicine, Surgery, Family Medicine, and Internal Medicine. It also serves as a rotation site for numerous residency programs from the University of Minnesota, including specialties such as otolaryngology, obstetrics/gynecology, orthopedics, neurosurgery, neurology, ophthalmology, and various medical subspecialty fellowships. Additionally, HCMC has independent fellowship programs in geriatrics, critical care medicine, and sleep medicine. The hospital provides internship opportunities for students from UCIMED, a medical school in Costa Rica, through an agreement signed in February 2006. Many UCIMED students later become residents at HCMC. HCMC also delivers emergency medical services (EMS) to parts of Minneapolis, Minnetonka, Golden Valley, and Shorewood, as well as serving as the EMS provider for Eden Prairie, St. Louis Park, Hopkins, St. Anthony, Woodland, Excelsior, Deephaven, Tonka Bay, Richfield, and most of Minnetonka south of Interstate 394. Its EMS fleet includes 19 ambulances, 3 medical director vehicles, and 2 supervisor units, as of January 2005. Additionally, a mass casualty incident (MCI) trailer is available for emergencies within its coverage area. In 2007, HCMC was projected to handle over 60,000 911 calls.
